key_insight: Strong adverse-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers still show component-wise outer similarity when each mean-defect or Reynolds-stress profile is normalized by its value at a common outer location.
engineering_relevance: This gives a compact reference for comparing and modeling APG boundary layers, helping turbulence-model validation and profile reconstruction in strong non-equilibrium flows.
method: Built a benchmark from DNS of a suction–blowing separation bubble plus published APG profiles.
Tested two mean-velocity defects and four Reynolds-stress components across wide ranges of Clauser parameter and Reynolds number.
Normalized each quantity by its value at a common outer location y_s, using y_s = 0.5δ for the main presentation.
evidence_signal: Across β_e = 0.04–180 and Re_θ = 530–19000, the normalized profiles collapse in the outer layer, with velocity-defect collapse for y/δ ≳ 0.2 and Reynolds-stress collapse for y/δ ≳ 0.4.
watch_item: The similarity is component-wise and outer-region dependent, so it does not imply a single universal scaling valid throughout the full boundary layer or for all APG configurations.
paper_title: Component-wise outer similarity of turbulent boundary layers with strong adverse-pressure gradient
